page: Microsoft Azure D128ds_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 512.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 7559 GB, and the instance does not include any GPUs. The CPU architecture is x86_64, featuring a 480 MB L3 cache and support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Benchmark data places this server in the top tier (top 10%) for multi-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. It also achieves top-tier results in memory bandwidth for both small cached and large uncached read/write blocks, as well as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and static web serving throughput. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core and PassMark memory scores ranking in the average (middle 50%) category. In LLM inference tests, the server shows strong prompt processing speeds but drops to average performance during text generation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D128ds_v7 offers high resource density, combining massive compute capacity with substantial local storage on a single instance. The tradeoff lies in its single-core performance and memory latency characteristics, which are average compared to specialized compute- or memory-optimized instances. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database operations, high-throughput web serving, multi-threaded data compression, and enterprise-level general-purpose workloads that require a balance of high-core-count processing and local storage capacity.
